subject.title: [Bug]: ACP session poisoned by API error — --resume replays error causing infinite loop

question: Which ACP failures should be allowed to discard an existing persisted conversation automatically?
rationale: A generic turn failure can mean either corrupt resume state or a transient/provider configuration problem; automatically dropping context is destructive, while matching user-facing error strings is brittle and provider-specific.

options.title: Use structured unrecoverable-session errors
options.body: Extend the ACP/acpx boundary to classify confirmed persisted-session corruption, rotate only for that class, and keep ordinary provider failures bound.

options.title: Unbind matching textual errors
options.body: Rotate sessions when selected model or similar error text appears, accepting false positives and dependency-message drift.

options.title: Recovery through explicit reset only
options.body: Do not auto-rotate failed turns; instead guarantee that `/reset` fully clears runtime and persistent ACP state.

recommendation.title: Use structured unrecoverable-session errors
recommendation.body: Extend the ACP/acpx boundary to classify confirmed persisted-session corruption, rotate only for that class, and keep ordinary provider failures bound.

likelyOwner.reason: The available routing evidence points to adjacent ACP lifecycle work, though primary control-plane ownership remains uncertain.
